short: A highly advanced American heavy bomber that waged a devastating strategic bombing campaign against Japan and delivered the atomic bombs.
full:
The Boeing B-29 Superfortress was an exceptionally advanced American heavy bomber introduced in 1944. Representing an enormous leap in aviation technology, it featured a pressurized cabin, dual-wheeled tricycle landing gear, and a sophisticated remote-controlled machine gun turret system. Built primarily for the Pacific theatre, its immense range allowed it to strike the Japanese home islands from bases in the Marianas, undertaking both high-altitude precision attacks and devastating low-level incendiary raids on wooden cities.

The immense cost of the B-29 programme far exceeded that of the Manhattan Project, reflecting its complexity and scale. Modified "Silverplate" variants of the aircraft dropped the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945, cementing its place in history. The Superfortress remained in front-line service through the early years of the Cold War, seeing extensive combat during the Korean War before being retired in 1960.
